transform.orientationEvidence: Source muzzle is at source -X (thin 3.5 cm flash hider; the 15.6 cm tall stock is at +X) and the concept-matching side (rendered from -Z it reproduces the muzzle-right concept) faces source -Z. The concept shows the rifle's RIGHT side, so placing it on -X with muzzle -Z requires a mirror: x'=z, y'=y, z'=x (det -1, winding flipped, handedness of the prop reversed).

dimensionsMeters.chosen: overall length 0.92 m (uniform scale; other dimensions follow source proportions)

conventions.referenceSide: -X (side seen by a right-handed first-person camera)

Muzzle.method: Barrel = dense-source vertices in the front 4 cm whose height is within 2.8 cm of the front-most top; tip z = min z of those; x/y = centre of the barrel cross-section within 1 cm of the tip.

Grip.method: Bottom profile (5 mm bins along Z): magazine = deepest run; pistol grip = deepest bin behind it and ahead of the rear 25% (stock); receiver bottom = highest underside between them; Grip = centroid of dense vertices in the grip run 1-6 cm below the receiver bottom (upper grip, just behind the trigger).

barrelAlignment.pitchMethod: Theil-Sen slope of the barrel top line (1 cm slice maxima) over 0-8% of the length from the muzzle (7 slices; top line range 1.8 mm). Level within this tolerance; no pitch rotation applied (concept profiles were level).

environmentTextures.normalMapNote: The procedural kit (reference/tools/procedural-environment-kit/generate_v2.py) encodes normal green as -dH/dv with v pointing image-down ("green down"). glTF/three.js expect green = image-up, so tiles rendered with the source maps light from the wrong vertical direction (grazing-light check: qa-artifacts/assets/props/procedural-normal-green-check.png). All extracted normal maps (and sign.glb) have the GREEN channel INVERTED to the glTF convention. Sources untouched.
environmentTextures.uvNote: Working-face textures are authored for one panel: UV 0..1 spans the whole face (sizes below). To tile level geometry at real scale, repeat every <uMeters> horizontally and <vMeters> vertically (or map a sub-range). They are NOT seamless by construction (noise/spots at the borders); joints are measured from pixels.
